titulo_es: La sílaba tónica y la tilde

intro.en: Notice which syllable is stressed and when Spanish writes an accent mark.

texto.en: Every Spanish word with more than one syllable has a stressed syllable. As a useful first guide, words ending in a vowel, **n** or **s** usually stress the next-to-last syllable; words ending in other consonants usually stress the last. A written accent mark shows exceptions, as in **café**, **lápiz** and **canción**. Words stressed on the antepenultimate syllable always carry an accent: **música**, **teléfono**. Question and exclamation words carry an accent mark even in indirect questions: **¿Qué quieres? / No sé qué quieres.** Compare **qué** with **que** in **Creo que sí**.

nota.en: Capital letters show the stressed syllable; the written accent is shown where needed.

frases.es: ¿Cómo se llama tu compañera? No sé qué libro quiere, pero creo que es una novela.
frases.en: What is your classmate’s name? I do not know which book she wants, but I think it is a novel.
